title: Quantum space-time is entangled and non-local at the Planck scale

statements.text: During a quantum computation, quantum space-time can be in an entangled state, so space-time itself is non-local at the Planck scale: all pixels are in a non-separable state and each loses its own identity.

sources.quote: During a quantum computational process, quantum space-time can be in an entangled state, which leads to non-locality of space-time itself at the Planck scale
